name: HAL Do-228

header.one_liner: Licence-built by HAL at Kanpur under a 1983 Dornier agreement, the Do-228 is a twin-turboprop light utility/maritime aircraft in service with the IAF, Indian Navy and Coast Guard; over 125 built, with fresh Coast Guard orders as recently as February 2026 and a civil Hindustan-228 variant flying UDAN routes.
header.maker: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Transport Aircraft Division, Kanpur (licence from Dornier / RUAG, Germany)
header.indigenous_label: Airframe licence-built by HAL Kanpur; Honeywell TPE331 engines and much avionics imported
header.mobility_or_class: Twin-turboprop light utility / maritime patrol aircraft (STOL, ~19-seat class)

at_a_glance.Indian_operators: Indian Air Force, Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard

what_it_is.prose: The Do-228 is a German-origin twin-turboprop STOL light utility aircraft that Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has licence-produced in India since the 1980s. HAL acquired production rights through a licence-production and phased technology-transfer agreement with Dornier in November 1983 and rolled out its first Kanpur-built aircraft in 1985. By 2014 HAL had manufactured around 125 aircraft, and later trade reporting cites more than 150 military Do-228 produced in India. The type serves across three Indian services — the Indian Air Force (communication, light transport, training), the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard (maritime surveillance and patrol) — powered by two imported Honeywell/Garrett TPE331 turboprops. The platform remains in active procurement: the Ministry of Defence signed a Rs 2,312 crore contract with HAL on 12 February 2026 for eight Dornier 228 aircraft for the Indian Coast Guard under the Buy (Indian) category, following an earlier Rs 458.87 crore contract for two ICG Dornier signed on 7 July 2023 that added glass cockpit, maritime patrol radar and an electro-optic/infra-red sensor. A civil derivative, the Hindustan-228, was certified in 2017 and entered scheduled service with Alliance Air on the Dibrugarh–Pasighat route on 12 April 2022 — described as the first Indian-made aircraft used for civil aviation operations — supporting regional-connectivity (UDAN) flying. The Atlas treats the Do-228 as a licence-built platform with a genuine and continuing HAL manufacturing role, without converting local production into an unsupported indigenous-content percentage given the imported engine and avionics content.

deployments_procurement.summary: The Do-228 is one of HAL's longest-running production lines, sustaining the Kanpur Transport Aircraft Division across military and, since 2022, civil orders. The most recent order is the February 2026 MoD contract for eight Coast Guard aircraft (Rs 2,312 crore, Buy (Indian)). Earlier Indian orders include two ICG aircraft in 2023 (Rs 458.87 crore) and, per Wikipedia, a 2015 contract for 14 Do-228 for the IAF (Rs 1,090 crore). The type equips the IAF, Indian Navy and Coast Guard, and now underpins a civil UDAN variant.

faq.question: Who builds the Do-228 in India and how many have been made?
faq.answer: HAL builds the Do-228 under a Dornier licence at its Transport Aircraft Division in Kanpur, having signed the agreement in November 1983 and rolled out its first aircraft in 1985. HAL had manufactured about 125 aircraft by 2014, and later trade reporting cites more than 150 military Do-228 produced in India.

faq.question: Which Indian services operate the Do-228?
faq.answer: The Indian Air Force, Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard all operate HAL-built Do-228s, in roles from light transport and communication to maritime surveillance and patrol. The Coast Guard remains an active buyer, with an eight-aircraft order signed in February 2026.

faq.question: Is the Do-228 indigenous?
faq.answer: No. It is a German (Dornier) design licence-built by HAL. The airframe is produced in Kanpur, but the two TPE331 engines are imported from Honeywell (USA) and much of the maritime mission avionics is imported, so it is not an indigenous-design platform.

faq.question: What is the civil Hindustan-228?
faq.answer: The Hindustan-228 is the civil-certified 17/19-seat derivative of HAL's Do-228. It was certified in 2017 and entered scheduled service with Alliance Air on the Dibrugarh–Pasighat route on 12 April 2022 under India's UDAN regional-connectivity scheme — described as the first Indian-made aircraft used in civil aviation operations.
